---
title: "House Prices: End-to-End Regression Case Study"
description: "End-to-end machine learning workflow for predicting residential property prices using structured tabular data."
---

## Overview

This project develops an end-to-end machine learning workflow for predicting residential property prices using the Kaggle House Prices dataset.

Rather than focusing solely on leaderboard performance, the project emphasizes the complete regression modeling process, including exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, feature transformations, model comparison, and rigorous evaluation through cross-validation.

The final objective is to build a predictive model capable of estimating house sale prices from structured property information and generating a valid Kaggle competition submission.

---

## Problem Statement

Given a set of residential property characteristics, the system must:

1. Explore and understand the dataset.
2. Prepare and engineer meaningful predictive features.
3. Train and compare multiple regression models.
4. Predict house sale prices for unseen properties.

---

## Methodology

The project follows a structured machine learning pipeline:

- Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
- Data cleaning and missing value treatment
- Feature engineering
- Log transformation of skewed variables
- Baseline models
- Linear regression
- Random Forest regression
- Gradient Boosting regression
- Cross-validation and model comparison
- Final model training and Kaggle submission

---

## Dataset

The project uses the **House Prices: Advanced Regression Techniques** dataset from Kaggle.

The dataset contains detailed information describing residential properties in Ames, Iowa, including:

- Lot characteristics
- Building quality and condition
- Interior and exterior features
- Garage and basement information
- Sale price (training set)

The objective is to predict the sale price of houses in the test set.
